## SECTION 19 — This Day in History (Global)
*   In 1945, Japan formally signed the Instrument of Surrender to the Allied nations aboard the USS Missouri, marking the end of World War II.
*   Also in 1945, Vietnamese leader Ho Chi Minh declared Vietnam's independence from France, forming the Democratic Republic of Vietnam.
*   The Great Fire of London began on this day in 1666, burning for three days and destroying a significant portion of the city, including St. Paul's Cathedral and approximately 13,000 houses.
*   The United States Department of the Treasury was founded on September 2, 1789.
*   In 1752, the United Kingdom adopted the Gregorian calendar, skipping 11 days to align with much of Western Europe.
*   In 31 BC, the naval Battle of Actium took place, where Octavian's forces defeated those of Mark Antony and Cleopatra, ending the Final War of the Roman Republic.
*   Cicero launched the first of his "Philippicae" (oratorical attacks) on Mark Antony in 44 BC.
*   In 1901, US Vice President Theodore Roosevelt used the phrase, "Speak softly and carry a big stick" at the Minnesota State Fair.
*   The first election of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile occurred in 1960, a date observed by the Tibetan community as Democracy Day.
*   CBS Evening News became the first U.S. network television's half-hour weeknight news broadcast in 1963, extending from 15 to 30 minutes.
